ST12000NM0007.window_type: Flat 10-Day Window (z-score normalised, healthy drives only)
ST12000NM0007.description: Kernel-based one-class classifier trained exclusively on healthy drive data. Fits a high-dimensional RBF hypersphere around the normal SMART distribution. Test drives falling outside the boundary are flagged as anomalies. Training subsampled to 5000 healthy drives for kernel tractability. Features z-score normalised (required for RBF kernel distance calculations). nu parameter set to 2x empirical failure rate as the expected contamination fraction.

ST12000NM0007.description: Density-based novelty detection. Measures how isolated each drive is relative to its k=20 nearest healthy neighbors in SMART feature space. A drive in a sparse region (far from similar drives) receives a high LOF score. Unlike global methods (OC-SVM, IF), LOF captures local density variations — effective when different drive failure modes cluster in distinct regions.

ST12000NM0007.description: Fits a robust multivariate Gaussian (Minimum Covariance Determinant) to the PCA-reduced healthy drive SMART distribution. Flags drives whose Mahalanobis distance from the Gaussian center exceeds the fitted threshold. PCA(30) applied first to handle high-dimensional SMART feature space (190 features). Formally tests: 'does this drive follow the same statistical distribution as healthy drives?' — the cleanest statistical formulation of normality.

ST12000NM0007.description: Feed-forward autoencoder (encoder: 190->92->46->23, decoder: mirror). Trained for 15 epochs exclusively on healthy drives. Anomaly score = mean squared reconstruction error per drive. Threshold set at 95th percentile of healthy training reconstruction errors. Failing drives exhibit SMART patterns the network never learned, producing high reconstruction error. Most interpretable neural anomaly detection approach.
